hook: NASA Voyager 1 just reached one light-day away, the time light takes to travel 24 hours.

sections.voiceover: NASA Voyager 1 just reached one light-day away, the time light takes to travel 24 hours.
sections.visual_cue: Deep space visualization showing the probe moving away from the Sun.

sections.voiceover: On November 18, 2026, the spacecraft hit this milestone after traveling for nearly 50 years. This 16 billion mile gap is massive, but how does NASA keep communicating with the probe?
sections.visual_cue: Archival footage of the Voyager 1 launch sequence.

sections.voiceover: However, Voyager 1 has pushed 26 billion kilometers into interstellar space beyond the Sun's protective bubble.
sections.visual_cue: Animation of the heliopause transition into deep interstellar space.

sections.voiceover: Light from our planet now takes 24 hours to reach the probe's sensors. Voyager 1 continues its lonely journey through the dark.
sections.visual_cue: Digital interface simulation showing a 24-hour signal delay timer.

sections.voiceover: Voyager 1 remains a single point of light in the silence.
sections.visual_cue: Voyager 1 drifting into the distant starfield.
